title: Speed, Verification and Trust
text:
Information now travels faster than verification can keep pace with it. A claim that circulates widely within minutes may take days to be corrected, and the correction rarely reaches the same audience. Journalists therefore face a difficult trade-off between immediacy and accuracy, since being first often rewards them more than being right.

Some researchers argue that the problem lies less in deliberate deception than in the structure of attention itself, which favours novelty and emotional intensity. Others counter that audiences are more discerning than critics assume, and that scepticism is widely practised. Whichever view is correct, the burden of judgement increasingly falls on individual readers, who must decide quickly what to trust.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what happens to corrections of widely circulated claims?
options: They reach the same audience quickly
They rarely reach the same audience
They appear before the original claim

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do some researchers say the problem lies in?
options: The structure of attention, which favours novelty and emotional intensity

questions.text: Why do journalists face a difficult trade-off, according to the passage?
options: Because accuracy is no longer valued
Because being first often rewards them more than being right

questions.text: What does the passage imply about responsibility for judging information?
options: It increasingly falls on individual readers
It has been removed by new technology
